articles.title: How SNL’s ‘Sister’ sketch is forcing families to confront unequal caregiving
articles.summary: The first time Mary McFarland saw the “Sister” sketch that aired on “Saturday Night Live” on Nov.
articles.body: The first time Mary McFarland saw the “Sister” sketch that aired on “Saturday Night Live” on Nov. 14, she laughed. She sent it to her siblings on impulse, thinking it was funny. “Then nobody responded. I’m like, ‘What have I done?’” she tells TODAY.com. But the more McFarland watched the sketch, the less funny it became. It resurfaced the story that played out 20 years before, when her mother moved in with her as McFarland herself was navigating Stage 3 cancer. Watching the sketch and thinking back to the turmoil between her and her siblings toward the end of her mother’s life, she wondered: “Maybe somebody should have been taking care of me.” The sketch landed on “Saturday Night Live” on Nov. 14 with a culture-moving thud. The gist? An advertisement for a product that will swoop in and solve all caregiving issues — a sister. The sketch points to the burden of caretaking that so often, but not always, falls on women. One of the three writers, Streeter Seidell, dedicated the sketch to his sister Heidi. “Sister is a live-in, 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free and also your sister,” host John Mulaney says in the spoof commercial. “Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs, because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life.” Since its debut, “Sister” has provoked a seismic response, both publicly and in family group chats. One Threads user said the video is causing chaos. “I started an entire family fight over this video today by sending it to my uncle,” the post read. The Painful Reality For many, “Sister” is exposing or affirming pre-existing (and sometimes painful) dynamics between siblings. Psychologist Adriana DeAmicis said in an email to TODAY.com “every single one” of her female clients has brought up the sketch in their sessions since it came out. “The humor gave women permission to laugh at something that is often deeply frustrating: being expected to take responsibility for everyone else’s needs while watching their brothers receive praise for doing far less,” DeAmicis said. “However, many women have been discussing this week how quickly they moved from laughing into feeling the true pain of a deep-seated and rarely acknowledged wound,” DeAmicis added. In sibling group chats, what’s meant to be a funny re-share is sparking real conversations and escalating tensions over the share of the caregiving load. Christine Pruden, who spent six years caretaking for her parents, sent her brother the sketch. “Ha!” his reply said. “Happy Sunday.” Pruden, who had been “blown away” by the sketch, says his reaction seemed small compared to hers. “It says everything so many of us women feel and never were really allowed to express, because if you do, you’re a troublemaker or a drama queen,” Pruden says of the sketch. Pruden wrote back, “I think there’s gonna be a lot of families talking about that skit over Thanksgiving dinner. Hits way too close to home for some of us eldest daughters and sisters.” “He didn’t have any response to that,” she says. Kimberly Wiener, who quit her job four years ago to care for her disabled elderly mother, sent the video to a group chat that included her seven siblings. She got no response other than a few laugh emoji and a private message from a sister-in-law who asked her if “the boys” would feel guilty by the sketch. “My reply was, ‘Don’t care — I am at the “see you at the funeral” stage,’” Wiener wrote in an email to TODAY.com, referencing a line from the sketch. Stacie Kowalski, who took a year of leave from her job while her father was dying, felt a tinge of worry after sending it to her brother. “I sort of thought, ‘Oh I hope he doesn’t get mad.’ Then I thought just how ridiculous that thought was — once again putting someone else’s feelings before mine,” she said in an email to TODAY.com. Kowalski’s brother did not respond, which, she said, “is a response.” Heather Lister said her brother laugh-reacted to the video. She hopes it provided “some eye-opening perspective” for other brothers. “What is so funny to me is how it is just assumed by the older generations, as well, that we daughters will do it,” she said in an email. Sparking Conversation — and Hopefully, Change For others actively caring for their parents, “Sister” is inspiring change. Kathryn Hinchey Wise said in a statement to TODAY.com that “Sister” “gave her the nerve to say what I’d been carrying for months.” She texted “Sister” in a group chat with her brothers, asking, “Did you watch the whole thing?” When she got no response, she wrote again, saying she wanted her brothers’ assistance moving their father to an assisted living floor in his building. “That message started a knock-down, drag-out fight,” she said, one that ended in her stepping back from being her father’s primary caretaker. “It wasn’t the outcome I wanted, but it was the one I needed,” she said. Rebecca Cynamon-Murphy, a 49-year-old from the Chicago suburbs, gathered the courage to text her brothers to have a meeting about what had to change moving forward. She shared the text exchange on Threads. “The text was an impulsive, inspired action after watching the sketch a second time,” Cynamon-Murphy said in a statement to TODAY.com. “My 2 sisters-in-law jumped into the group chat immediately to hold them accountable and they are rock-stars.” A meeting, Cynamon-Murphy says, has been set. Tanya Eby, meanwhile, received a text from her brother the day after she sent him the “Sister” sketch, specifically to talk about care for their mother, who has Alzheimer’s disease. Together, Eby says, they “came up with a plan” that eases her load and increases his. “What the sketch did for me was affirm that I wasn’t imagining these assumed roles. I wasn’t being hysterical. It really wasn’t fair,” she tells TODAY.com. “It empowered me to be really firm in boundaries. Instead of saying, ‘Oh, I know you’re going through a lot. Don’t worry, I’ll take care of it.’ It allowed me to say, ‘I hear you. This is hard. I still need help with this.’” Eby, who was developing resentment toward her brother, says she hopes the conversation sparked by the sketch can improve their relationship moving forward. Meanwhile, for those navigating sibling estrangement, “Sister” is a reminder of the siblings who aren’t there anymore. Lia Prusha, a therapist, texted it to both of her half-brothers from whom she is estranged, in part because of her experience caring for their late parents. Prusha says she hasn’t received a response. “I think my sending it is being defiant. You can’t make me invisible. I’m a worthwhile person and I exist,” she says. The Caregiver Crisis It’s worth noting that not all “sisters” are actually sisters. Scott Lerman told TODAY.com in an email that his father turned to him after watching the sketch and said, “Oh my God, you’re the sister.” “They know exactly who I am in our family,” he said. Eliza Salerno, president and COO at Medical Guardian, a company that helps older adults live safely and independently at home, isn’t surprised by the earthquake this sketch caused. “It’s inevitable that the caregiver crisis and the things going on with caregivers (becomes) a broader conversation topic because of the amount of people in the country having to step into the role,” she says. According to an AARP survey, 63 million Americans are caregivers in 2025, up 50% since 2015. Salerno says the crisis is due to the “silver tsunami” — the rapid aging of the U.S. population — healthcare issues, and the changing structure of the family unit, due to two-party working households. “There’s not enough time in the day to work, take care of kids, live your life and manage this now really new thing that’s occurring,” she says. It’s making younger women factor the reality of the “Sister” sketch into their future plans. At 31, Olivia Landon has already done her fair share of caretaking, sitting by her grandma’s and great aunt’s deathbeds and putting her life on hold for her mother’s spinal surgery recovery for two weeks, even though her dad was at home. She told TODAY.com in a statement she texted “Sister” to her family, who “ignored it.” Landon is now deliberately living in New Orleans, too far for her to keep caretaking. “Leaving is the only way out,” Landon said. McFarland, meanwhile, spoke to her own daughter in the aftermath of “Sister” about their future. McFarland moved to Oklahoma to be closer to her daughter and grandkids and says she now has a “lovely” family dynamic. “She’s like, ‘Mom, of course I’m here for you, and I want to be here for you,’” McFarland says.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI understands just how important a smartphone is
articles.summary: GTA 6 features an incredibly realistic virtual phone that’s embedded into much of the open-world game.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI, in many ways, tries to simulate real life. And life in 2026 would not be complete without a smartphone. GTA VI understands this and makes the phone not just a central part of the experience, but an object that exists within the world. You may try to escape into a fantasy of robbing banks and fighting drug lords, but you can’t get away from texts from your mom or nagging fitness app notifications. Seeing a smartphone in a game isn’t a new phenomenon. The device has become a natural stand-in for the main menu in many games, giving players an interface that feels intuitive, because a phone is something they use every day. But the phone in GTA VI is different for a few reasons. One is that it behaves much like any other object in the game, whether it’s a gun or a bottle of beer. The action doesn’t pause when you use your phone. Instead, the game switches to a first-person viewpoint, where you can still walk around — or drive, if you’re feeling ambitious — while reading texts or flipping through a fictional version of Instagram. Rob Nelson, the co-studio head at developer Rockstar North and producer on GTA VI, says that it would’ve felt “archaic” to have a static phone that worked like those in other games, or the one in GTA V, which appeared as a pop-up at the bottom of the screen across from the minimap. “We felt that it was important to make it physical so you have to look at it and put your attention on it, including while driving,” he explains. “It’s about finding the line between realism and player convenience. But the act of being lost in your phone felt like something worth doing, even though it could mean slightly more inconvenience. In this game you are committing to using it.” (Of course, texting and driving, like much of what you do in GTA VI, is both very dangerous and very illegal.) You have to interact with the phone in the game constantly. Often the story plays out through phone calls and text messages, and you have a surprisingly large array of apps to use that serve a real purpose in the game. You manage your money in a banking app, use a rideshare app when you need a lift, track your workouts in a fitness app, scroll through a social network complete with comments and the ability to like posts, and sideload an AI tool that scans nearby cars so you can see how easy they’ll be to steal. You can even change the wallpaper and ringtone. (GTA VI has two main characters that you swap between, and each has their own phone, though they’re functionally identical.) [Image: What’s most impressive is how all of these apps interact with each other. For instance, after pulling off a major heist, a friend might text you a news story about it, asking “was this you!?” You can then click the link, open up the news app, and read an actual article about what went down. These kinds of interactions can be functional, like when another character texts you a location, which you can then add to your map so the GPS can guide you there. Other times, they add texture to the world or depth to the characters. GTA VI is a love story about two criminals named Jason and Lucia, and you play as both. At one point, while controlling Lucia, I got a text asking for a selfie. I opened up the camera, shot a pic of Lucia drinking a latte, and sent it over. Jason replied immediately — and their relationship got a boost. Phones are so fully integrated into the game that they can even interrupt the characters’ sleep. At the end of each day, you can click on a bed to rest for the night. But neither Jason nor Lucia will instantly fall asleep when you do — instead, they’ll sit down and pull out their phone, and you have the option to doomscroll or catch up on texts instead of going to sleep right away. Nelson says that this was implemented because the developers wanted to include the ability for the characters to sit on the bed at night, much like a real couple in a shared living space might do. “We needed something to do aside from just sitting there staring at nothing,” he says. If nothing else, GTA VI’s phone shows how alike we all are: Even bank robbers being hunted by the police can’t seem to stop scrolling. “Phones are a constant part of our lives,” Nelson says of the evolution, “even more than they were in 2013.”

articles.title: 'JAG' actor Larry Poindexter dead at 66
articles.summary: Actor Larry Poindexter died Wednesday while awaiting surgery for broken ribs days after being struck by a car in Los Angeles; no cause of death released.
articles.body: Actor Larry Poindexter died Wednesday awaiting surgery days after being struck by a car in Los Angeles. He was 66. Poindexter, a character actor known for roles on such television shows as "JAG" and "Days of Our Lives," died suddenly Wednesday morning in a hospital while awaiting surgery to repair broken ribs sustained in the crash, as Deadline first reported. He had been struck by a vehicle Friday while crossing a street in his Studio City neighborhood to pick up food. An official cause of death has not been released. Poindexter is survived by his wife Carol Kritzer and their twin sons, Rees and Jake. HOLLYWOOD STARS WE'VE LOST IN 2026 Paul Iacono, who played the title role of RJ Berger on the 2010-2011 MTV comedy series "The Hard Times of RJ Berger," posted a tribute to Poindexter, who played his father on the show. "I’m heartbroken by the loss of Larry Poindexter, my dad on RJ Berger," Iacono wrote on Instagram on Thursday morning. "He was opinionated, to say the least, and I loved him for it. When I was in my early twenties, Larry looked out for me in ways I didn’t fully appreciate at the time. He offered wisdom I wasn’t always ready to hear, and it took me a few years to realize just how right he was about so many things. He taught me that being a good person and collaborator mattered just as much as being a great actor. "I’m forever honored to have played his son, and I’ll always cherish him as my second father. ❤️" LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: Attempted murder arrest after Bradford councillor stabbed
articles.summary: Bradford Moor councillor Ibrar Ali is in hospital with serious injuries.
articles.body:
A councillor has been seriously injured after being stabbed while undertaking his duties in Bradford.

Bradford Moor councillor Ibrar Ali was attacked at about 11:04 GMT on Manse Street, according to the deputy leader of Your Bradford Independent Group, councillor Ishtiaq Ahmed.

West Yorkshire Police said a 32-year-old man had been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and was being held in custody.

The force added there was "no information to suggest that this is a politically motivated incident at this time".

Ali is believed to have been injured on Thornbury Avenue, before being driven to the nearby Manse Street where emergency services attended, according to police.

A force spokesperson previously said the suspect had climbed on to the roof of a property on Thornbury Avenue following the incident and was later brought down.

Ahmed said Ali was undergoing emergency surgery at Leeds General Infirmary after being stabbed in the leg. He said Ali was in a stable condition but had lost a lot of blood.

"My thoughts are with him and his family and loved ones. It's an extremely distressing time," said Ahmed.

"We shouldn't have to fear for our personal safety because we have chosen to serve the public.

"There should be no normalisation of violence in our democratic life."

Responding to the incident in his Bradford East constituency, Labour MP Imran Hussain described the incident as "horrific" and "deeply disturbing".

"My thoughts and prayers are with councillor Ibrar Ali and his family," said Hussain.

"No elected politician should feel under threat or fear for their safety while carrying out their duties and serving their community."

Ch Supt Richard Padwell urged anyone with information to contact police.

"This is a serious incident where a local councillor has been stabbed in the street and our thoughts are with him, his family and colleagues at this difficult time," he said.

"Whilst the investigation is in the early stages, there is nothing to suggest that this incident is politically motivated at this time."

Ali is a community development manager at charity The Leap.

He has worked with community organisations Bradford Moor Pass and was one of the founders of Leeds Road Festival.

He was first elected as a councillor in the May local election, replacing the previous Labour representatives.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney is being linked to the next James Bond movie. She has some big names backing her.
articles.summary: Two former Bond actors have endorsed Sweeney for a role opposite Robert Pattinson, while her ties to Jeff Bezos have fueled speculation.
articles.body:
Now that Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the next James Bond , speculation has shifted to his potential costars — and Sydney Sweeney is emerging as a possible contender.

The 29-year-old actor has received public backing from two former Bond stars, Trina Parks and Jane Seymour, and Variety reported last October that Sweeney's involvement was "something Amazon founder Jeff Bezos reportedly wants very much to happen." Amazon MGM Studios oversees the Bond franchise, and Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in Pattinson's casting .

Variety's Ellise Shafer described Sweeney as a "Bond Girl no-brainer" in an article published Monday, suggesting she is "likely to be at the top of Amazon's list."

Sweeney has become one of Hollywood's most prominent young actors, building on her breakout role in HBO's Euphoria with leading parts in the romantic comedy Anyone but You , the psychological thriller The Housemaid and the boxing drama Christy .

Shafer highlighted Sweeney's physical transformation for Christy , which involved months of training and a 30-pound weight gain. Although Sweeney has yet to star in a major action film, Shafer suggested Bond could be "the perfect chance for her to flex that muscle." However, she questioned whether the actor "could match Pattinson's zany personality."

In an October 2025 interview with Variety , Sweeney said she was unfamiliar with the rumors, though she had long been a fan of the franchise.

Asked whether she would consider appearing in a Bond film, she replied, "Depends on the script." She then joked, "I think I'd have more fun as James Bond."

Director Paul Feig, who worked with Sweeney on The Housemaid , told U.K. newspaper the Sun in April that he would "rather Sydney be the next Bond." "There have been some cool Bond girls, but come on, let her be the super-spy, she's great," he added.

Women have played central roles in the Bond franchise since Ursula Andress appeared as Honey Ryder in 1962's Dr. No . More recent films have featured women in prominent action roles, including Lashana Lynch as Nomi, an MI6 agent who inherited the 007 designation in No Time to Die .

Trina Parks, who played Thumper opposite Sean Connery in 1971's Diamonds Are Forever , endorsed the idea in an interview with the Telegraph last month. "Sydney would do a wonderful job," Parks said, calling her a "talented actress" with a "Hollywood classic kind of style and poise."

She added, "I feel for modern cinema and film-making and the future of Bond, audiences want to see a woman opposite Bond who is independent and has ownership of her sexuality. Sydney has those qualities."

Jane Seymour, who played Solitaire opposite Roger Moore in 1973's Live and Let Die , said in June that she was "sure" Sweeney would be a good "Bond girl." She said, "I mean, she is gorgeous, talented. Why not?"

Beyond the endorsements, Sweeney's ties to Bezos have fueled speculation. Sweeney attended Bezos's wedding to Lauren Sánchez Bezos in Venice in June 2025, and in January 2026 the actor launched a lingerie brand with financial backing linked to Bezos . Amazon MGM is set to produce her upcoming movie Split Fiction .

In November 2025, Sánchez Bezos applauded Sweeney's performance in Christy , calling it "Oscar-worthy" in an Instagram story. "I have to say it's one of the most powerful movies I have ever seen," she added.

Pattinson was named on Monday as the next 007, succeeding Daniel Craig, who stepped down after 2021's No Time to Die . Bezos participated in the selection process for the next 007 alongside director Denis Villeneuve, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and Amazon MGM executives.

According to the Times of London , Sánchez Bezos was said to have supported Pattinson. An unnamed Los Angeles producer told the newspaper that Bezos had shared footage with his wife as the process progressed.

The producer said three people connected to the business had described Sánchez Bezos as particularly enthusiastic about Pattinson, believing he had "the look, sex appeal and talent" needed to deliver as Bond.

articles.title: Jax Taylor, former ‘Vanderpump Rules’ and Bravo reality TV star, reveals cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Jax Taylor, who was made famous on the Bravo reality series “Vanderpump Rules,” shared with fans Thursday that he was recently diagnosed with cancer.
articles.body: Jax Taylor, who was made famous on the Bravo reality series “Vanderpump Rules,” shared with fans Thursday that he was recently diagnosed with cancer. Taylor, 47, wrote on his Instagram account that he’d been seeking treatment for what he believed was kidney stones in July when a CT scan showed a tumor above his left kidney. He sought care because he woke up one morning “in horrible pain,” he said, adding that the cancer was diagnosed after “many tests and appointments.” “I lost my father to cancer, so hearing that word just broke me,” Taylor wrote. “It put me in a really dark place.” The tumor was removed in a five-hour surgery, with Taylor saying the growth was larger than initially expected. He expressed his gratitude to medical staff at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, in Los Angeles, for all their care. Taylor described the ordeal as an eye-opening experience that reminded him how quickly life can change. In his statement, Taylor also noted that he will be two years sober next week and said he was proud of himself. “If there’s one thing I hope people can take away from this, it’s never to take your health for granted,” Taylor said. “I did for many years and I won’t ever do that again.” He did not provide additional details on his diagnosis or his prognosis. Taylor’s father died in 2017 just weeks after the reality star shared the diagnosis with his fans. He said at the time that he wouldn’t wish the disease on his worst enemy and described his father as his idol. “My dad was always the person who never got sick, I always looked up to him. I call him all the time,” Taylor said. “To see him so vulnerable, I’ve never seen him emotional my whole entire life.” Taylor was one of the first cast members to appear in Bravo’s “Vanderpump Rules,” a reality show that revolved around the employees of Lisa Vanderpump’s restaurants. The series was a 2013 spin-off of “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills,” which Vanderpump starred on for nine seasons. He met and married his fellow cast member Brittany Cartwright on the show. The couple were featured in another spinoff, “The Valley,” which followed a number of reality star families going through big changes. Taylor and Cartwright had one child together, a son, before separating in 2024. As of May, their divorce had not yet been finalized, according to Cartwright. There were growing concerns from viewers about Taylor’s behavior on the second season of “The Valley.” Cameras captured heated arguments between him and Cartwright before Taylor eventually checked himself into a mental health treatment facility. Cast members said they received angry messages from Taylor while he was in the facility. Cartwright told viewers that her husband would “rage text” her while there, adding that she worried that if he didn’t receive help he would continue to spiral. Taylor revealed that he was diagnosed with PTSD and bipolar disorder. The reality star has also been public with his past substance abuse issues, saying he specifically struggled with cocaine use. He announced last year that he would not return to “The Valley” as he prioritized his mental health.

articles.title: Katie Price's sister Sophie says she has 'no sympathy' for her after fourth nose job; model reveals undergoing MRI and ECG tests for unexplained weight loss
articles.summary: Former glamour model Katie Price has had another cosmetic procedure, undergoing what is believed to be her fourth nose job.
articles.body: Former glamour model Katie Price has had another cosmetic procedure, undergoing what is believed to be her fourth nose job. However, her latest surgery became a talking point on The Katie Price Show, the podcast she co-hosts with her sister Sophie, who made it clear that she was not particularly sympathetic about her sibling's decision to go under the surgeon's knife again.After Sophie showed Katie a nurse's hat made by her daughter, Katie jokingly asked whether her sister wanted to nurse her following the nose operation."You want to nurse me for my nose?" Katie asked.Sophie responded bluntly: "I don't got no sympathy for you."Katie, 48, clarified that she was not seeking sympathy and had not complained about her recovery. She also explained that the latest procedure was relatively minor and did not involve breaking her nose or requiring stitches."Didn't have it broken. Haven't got stitches. All I had is just narrowed it a bit. Keep this (the bandage) on for 10 days and it's off. So no stitches, no broken-ness, it was just a little bit wonky where I had that lip lift," she said.She further explained that the procedure was quick, adding: "So that was it. In and out. Done. Have this on four days and away we go."When Sophie asked about her experience after waking up from anaesthesia, Katie said she was discharged within an hour and had not developed bruising or noticeable swelling.Katie Price's history of cosmetic surgeriesKatie has been open about undergoing several cosmetic procedures over the years, including breast augmentation, facelifts, eyelid surgeries and lip enhancements.She previously confirmed having three nose operations. Her first rhinoplasty took place in 2007, when she was 29, to correct what she described as a "wonky" appearance. She underwent another procedure in 2023 after an earlier lip incision reportedly affected the shape of her nose.Last year, Katie travelled to Turkey for what was described as a mini nose lift, alongside facelift adjustments and ear-pinning surgery. Her latest procedure reportedly took place in Belgium earlier this month and involved narrowing her nose without breaking the bone or requiring stitches.Katie Price undergoes MRI and ECG tests over unexplained weight lossApart from discussing her latest cosmetic procedure, Katie also shared an update about her health, revealing that doctors are investigating her significant weight loss over recent months.Speaking to Sophie on The Katie Price Show, the 48-year-old said she has been advised to undergo an ECG, MRI scan and a bone examination to determine why she has become so thin."Funny enough, I've got to have an ECG, MRI scan, and a bone thing because obviously I've been to the doctors of why I'm losing weight and they want to get to the bottom of it," she said.Katie admitted that she does not want to remain at her current weight and hopes to regain some muscle through exercise."So yes, I've got to go and have an MRI, ECG to check my heart and check all in my body because I am skinny and I don't want to be this skinny. But hopefully now going to the gym and that I can build some muscle up," she added.She also revealed that she has low blood pressure, with doctors examining her condition to determine the appropriate course of action."I've got very low blood pressure. So the doctors are just seeing everything what they can do," she said.Doctors had earlier referred Katie Price to a gastroenterologistKatie's latest health update comes after she spoke about undergoing further medical investigations earlier this year. In January, she admitted being concerned about photographs showing her looking "gaunt" and sought medical advice to understand her weight loss.She later revealed that doctors had requested additional blood tests and referred her to a gastroenterologist, a specialist who treats digestive system conditions.Speaking on her podcast, she said: "The doctors have rang me. I've got to go back and have two more blood tests because I've got to see a gastroenterologist or something to get to the bottom of why I'm losing weight."Son Junior Price cooks for her after expressing concern over eating habitsKatie's weight loss has also worried her family. Her son Junior recently shared an Instagram video of himself preparing a large pasta meal for his mother, explaining that he wanted to make sure she was eating properly."Guys, normalise going to your mum's house and cooking them dinner," Junior said.Katie appreciated the gesture and praised his cooking, revealing that he had also prepared another meal for her to eat the following day.Junior, however, suggested that he had to take the initiative because his mother would otherwise not cook for herself."Otherwise she won't eat!" he said.Katie Price addresses Ozempic speculationDuring an appearance on Good Morning Britain in March, host Susanna Reid expressed concern about Katie's increasingly slim appearance."Katie, can I ask, because I am concerned about your weight. You are very, very, very, skinny," Susanna said.Katie acknowledged that she had lost considerable weight and admitted that she looked thinner than she wanted to."People that follow me online will know I have lost weight. I recognise I have lost weight. I look too skinny, I look gaunt," she said.She also addressed speculation that her appearance was linked to Ozempic, a weight-loss medication, saying doctors had ruled it out after examining her blood reports."I said to them, everyone said I am on Ozempic, they said, well we can tell in your bloods you're not," she explained.Katie further disclosed that she was lacking iron and experiencing perimenopause. articles.title: Muere atropellado a los 66 años Larry Poindexter, actor de 'Friends', 'CSI' y 'S.W.A.T.'
articles.standfirst: El intérprete estadounidense falleció el miércoles, cinco días después de ser arrollado por un coche en Los Ángeles
articles.summary: El intérprete estadounidense falleció el miércoles, cinco días después de ser arrollado por un coche en Los Ángeles
articles.body: El actor estadounidense Larry Poindexter ha fallecido a los 66 años, cinco días después de sufrir un atropello en Studio City, el barrio de Los Ángeles en el que residía. El intérprete, conocido por sus apariciones en series como 'Friends', 'CSI' y 'JAG', murió este miércoles, según ha informado el medio estadounidense Deadline. El accidente se produjo el 11 de noviembre de 2026, cuando Poindexter salió a comprar y fue atropellado por un automóvil mientras cruzaba la calle. Como consecuencia del impacto, sufrió varias lesiones y fracturas en las costillas, por lo que tuvo que ser trasladado a un hospital. Los médicos tenían previsto intervenirle el miércoles 18 de noviembre para tratar las fracturas. Sin embargo, su estado de salud empeoró repentinamente antes de que pudiera someterse a la operación. Por el momento, no han trascendido más detalles sobre las circunstancias de su fallecimiento. Nacido el 16 de diciembre de 1959 en Dallas, Larry Poindexter creció en una familia vinculada al mundo artístico. Su padre, H. R. Poindexter, fue diseñador de iluminación y escenografía y ganador de un premio Tony, mientras que su madre, Sue Ann Erdman, era cantante de ópera. Su carrera como actor comenzó en 1982, con una participación en un episodio de la serie 'A New Day in Eden'. Poco después debutó en el cine con 'Thursday's Child'. Uno de sus primeros papeles destacados llegó en 1984, cuando interpretó a Ben Welch durante 30 episodios de la ficción 'Days of Our Lives'. También formó parte del reparto de 'Santa Bárbara', donde encarnó a Justin Moore en 23 episodios. A lo largo de los años, el intérprete participó en numerosas producciones de la televisión estadounidense, entre ellas 'Días felices', 'Con ocho basta' y 'Los problemas crecen'. También tuvo papeles en 'General Hospital', donde dio vida a Asher Thomas, y en 'JAG', serie en la que interpretó a Dalton Lowne durante la tercera temporada. Uno de sus trabajos más reconocidos en la gran pantalla llegó en 2003 con 'S.W.A.T.: Los hombres de Harrelson', película en la que encarnó al capitán Tom Fuller, miembro del Departamento de Policía de Los Ángeles. Larry Poindexter también dejó su huella en algunas de las series más populares de la televisión. En 'Friends' interpretó al bombero Dave en el episodio 'The One with the Candy Hearts', emitido en 1995. Además, participó en la popular serie 'CSI', una de las numerosas producciones televisivas en las que intervino a lo largo de su trayectoria profesional. Su filmografía televisiva incluye asimismo apariciones en 'Bones', donde interpretó al senador Bethlehem en 2005; 'Cómo conocí a vuestra madre', en la que encarnó a Joe Donova en 2010, y 'El mentalista', donde dio vida a Quinton Bosh en 2012. Con una carrera iniciada a principios de los años ochenta y más de cuatro décadas de trayectoria, Larry Poindexter deja tras de sí una extensa lista de trabajos en cine y televisión, especialmente en algunas de las ficciones más conocidas de la pequeña pantalla estadounidense.

articles.title: Un microbús repleto de jóvenes modelos acapara todas las miradas en la fiesta de cumpleaños de LeonardoDiCaprio
articles.standfirst: El actor celebró sus 52 años en su mansión de Beverly Hills rodeado de estrellas como Jeff Bezos, Al Pacino y Tobey Maguire
articles.summary: El actor celebró sus 52 años en su mansión de Beverly Hills rodeado de estrellas como Jeff Bezos, Al Pacino y Tobey Maguire
articles.body: El actor Leonardo DiCaprio celebró su 52 cumpleaños con una fiesta por todo lo alto en su mansión de Beverly Hills. El intérprete estadounidense, que cumplió años el pasado 11 de noviembre, reunió a numerosas personalidades del cine, la música y otros ámbitos en una celebración privada. Uno de los detalles que más llamó la atención fue la llegada de un grupo de diez jóvenes en un microbús blanco, vestidas con looks de fiesta y tacones altos, según las imágenes difundidas por el medio Page Six. Entre ellas se encontraba Courtney Boerner, concursante del programa 'Love Island', que destacó con unos shorts muy cortos de color crudo, un corpiño blanco transparente y una chaqueta de cuero a juego, además de complementos rojos. El resto de las jóvenes, cuya identidad no ha trascendido, vestían mayoritariamente de negro. La celebración reunió a numerosos rostros conocidos. Entre los asistentes estuvieron Jeff Bezos y su esposa, Lauren Sánchez; Al Pacino; Tobey Maguire; Jonah Hill; Orlando Bloom y Justin Trudeau. También acudieron Casey Affleck junto a Caylee Cowan, Elizabeth Banks, Cara Delevingne y Travis Barker, que asistió acompañado de sus hijos, Landon y Alabama. El rapero 50 Cent fue otro de los protagonistas de la velada gracias a una actuación sorpresa. La posible ausencia de Vittoria Ceretti, pareja de Leonardo DiCaprio desde 2023, ha sido uno de los asuntos más comentados tras la celebración. Según fuentes citadas por la prensa del corazón del New York Post, la modelo italiana también habría asistido a la fiesta. Sin embargo, no aparece en las fotografías ni en los vídeos que han trascendido del evento, por lo que su presencia no ha podido confirmarse públicamente. Esta circunstancia ha dado pie a especulaciones sobre una posible crisis sentimental, aunque no existe ninguna confirmación de una ruptura ni de problemas en la relación. La comparación con el cumpleaños del año pasado también ha contribuido a alimentar los comentarios: entonces, Vittoria Ceretti sí fue fotografiada llevando la tarta del actor durante la celebración de sus 51 años. La relación entre ambos también ha despertado interés por la conocida fama de Leonardo DiCaprio de mantener relaciones con mujeres menores de 25 años. Vittoria Ceretti, sin embargo, tiene actualmente 28 AÑOS, una circunstancia que ha llevado a muchos a considerar que el actor habría roto esa supuesta regla. En agosto de 2025, durante una entrevista con la revista Esquire, el director Paul Thomas Anderson preguntó al protagonista de 'El lobo de Wall Street' qué edad tendría si no supiera cuántos años tiene. "Treinta y dos", respondió Leonardo DiCaprio en tono de broma, antes de añadir que, emocionalmente, había cumplido 35 el año anterior.

articles.title: Larry Poindexter, ‘Days of Our Lives’ and ‘S.W.A.T.’ actor, dies after being hit by car while crossing street
articles.summary: Veteran actor Larry Poindexter — who appeared in soap operas “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” and the movie “S.W.A.T.”
articles.body: Veteran actor Larry Poindexter — who appeared in soap operas “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” and the movie “S.W.A.T.” — died Wednesday, days after he was hit by a car while crossing the street near his Los Angeles home, officials said Thursday. He was 66. Poindexter was walking near the corner of Moorpark Street and Lankershim Boulevard on Friday, about three blocks from the actor’s home, when he was struck by a car at around 6 p.m. PT, his agent and police said. The investigation is ongoing, an LAPD spokesperson said. “He was picking up some dinner,” the actor’s agent, Harry Gold, told NBC News on Thursday. Poindexter suffered broken ribs but his injuries were not believed to be fatal, according to Gold. “They did not diagnose this as anything serious,” Gold said. “They put him in the hospital for observation and to repair some broken bones and then he passed away.” Gold praised his client’s work ethic and diverse skill set. “He had great musical talent, was in rock band and produced musicals,” Gold said. “That was important to him.” Poindexter’s long career includes 30 episodes on “Days of Our Lives” between 1984 and 2018 and a dozen appearances on “General Hospital” in 2005. He played by-the-book LAPD Capt. Tom Fuller in the 2003 movie “S.W.A.T.,” supervising Samuel L. Jackson’s Sgt. Dan “Hondo” Harrelson. “He offered wisdom I wasn’t always ready to hear, and it took me a few years to realize just how right he was about so many things,” Iacono wrote. “He taught me that being a good person and collaborator mattered just as much as being a great actor.” Iacono posted a picture of himself flanked by his on-screen parents, Poindexter and Beth Littleford, adding that: “I’m forever honored to have played his son, and I’ll always cherish him as my second father.” Poindexter is survived by his wife, casting director Carol Kritzer, and their twin boys, Rees and Jake.

articles.title: Blockbuster GTA VI release shows cultural, economic heft of video games
articles.summary: Runaway success of popular franchise comes as video game industry has struggled with mass layoffs in recent years.
articles.body:
Even before its release, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) was a cultural phenomenon that cemented the status of video games as the undisputed champion of the vaunted United States entertainment sector.

The game racked up more than $1.5bn in pre-sales before Thursday’s launch and attracted nonstop buzz and anticipation on social media, where players have waited more than 13 years since the last edition of the popular franchise was released.

“The launch of GTA VI is a reminder that games aren’t just niche entertainment—they’re now at the centre of global culture,” Mark DeLoura, Vice President of Strategy for GDC Festival of Gaming, told Al Jazeera in an email.

In GTA VI, players follow the journey of two characters, Jason and Lucia, as they explore the underworld of Vice City, a fictionalised version of Miami, Florida.

Almost impossibly, the newest addition seems to have lived up to more than a decade of hype: critics are nearly unanimous in their praise, with the latest GTA becoming the best-reviewed video game of all time.

That success is partly explained by the nostalgia that the game evokes for those who grew up playing it with friends, along with meticulous worldbuilding and attention to detail, memorable soundtracks, and the transgressive thrill of running pedestrians over in a semi-truck.

GTA’s appeal was only heightened by the fact that, for an earlier generation of gamers, parents, media coverage, and politicians were united in stern disapproval.

While most critics of violent video games have long since abandoned the field or switched sides in a bid for relevance with young voters, a few holdouts remain.

“I really am going to say I’m not thinking this is a good thing for our culture and society,” a member of a recent Fox News programme said of the game.

“They’ll have a documentary on how best to steal a car at gunpoint or shoot a cop,” Republican Representative Tim Burchett told the outlet TMZ, arguing that GTA encourages violence and lawbreaking. “I mean, what in the world!”

But across US culture and politics, the taboo has largely faded away.

Once the subject of television segments asking if it would corrupt impressionable youths by exposing them to a seedy underworld of carjackings and police shootouts, everyone from the US military and the White House to the Weather Channel has tapped into the runaway popularity of the game’s sixth instalment.

The US military outlet Task and Purpose reported that 43 soldiers took advantage of a reenlistment incentive that gave them a four-day weekend to enjoy the game’s release.

Assessments of GTA’s cultural impact have also shifted, with critics lauding the franchise’s ability to capture the pulse of life in the US and its exploration of themes such as the hardships faced by immigrants and minorities.

“When a release like this becomes a major cultural event in the US and a shared global conversation, it says a lot about both the scale of the games industry and the place games now hold in people’s lives,” said DeLoura from GDC Festival of Gaming.

According to the Entertainment Software Association, an industry group, about two-thirds of people in the US play video games, and the sector generated more than $95bn in economic activity in 2025, with US consumers spending more than $60bn on games.

By comparison, the 2025 North American box office for movie ticket sales was just under $9bn.

The runaway success of GTA VI comes, counterintuitively, at a time when the gaming industry is struggling to cope with a challenging financial environment and mass layoffs.

“The industry hired for a pandemic that ended. Demand stopped growing in 2022, costs didn’t, and the average blockbuster now costs $440m, up from $47m in 2000,” Joost van Dreunen, an adjunct assistant professor at NYU Stern and writer of the SuperJoost Playlist newsletter on Substack, said in an email.

“GTA VI proves that the model works for exactly one company,” he added, noting that the developer, Rockstar Games, spent a billion dollars and leaned on thousands of employees to create a level of attention to detail that few others can hope to match.

According to the tracker website Gaming Layoffs, 40 video game studios have shuttered in 2026 alone, with nearly 13,000 workers laid off. That figure represents a nearly 150 percent increase over the same time last year.

Life for some workers in the industry has also become more precarious.

A survey of industry workers by the GDC Festival of Gaming, compiled in a state-of-the-industry report in 2026, found that about 39 percent of US respondents had been laid off at least once in the last two years.

About 77 percent of US respondents also said they were “not hopeful” about the direction of the industry, and about 30 percent said they were considering leaving.

DeLoura from the GDC Festival of Gaming said the industry’s challenges have had “a real impact on a lot of very talented people”, but he remains optimistic the industry will weather the storm.

“The long arc of the game industry is one of strong growth,” he said.

“More people play games than ever, more people have access to them on the devices in their pockets, and more people can make and share games than at any point in history! To me, that’s the clearest way to understand this moment: not as a contradiction, but as a sign of how big, global, and varied games have become.”

articles.title: My boss canceled our 1:1 so I could keep playing ‘GTA’
articles.summary: Within the first 20 minutes of playing “GTA 6,” I’ve been Tased, driven a boat, ransacked a remote drug dealer’s compound, stolen their cash and made my getaway in a plane.
articles.body: Within the first 20 minutes of playing “GTA 6,” I’ve been Tased, driven a boat, ransacked a remote drug dealer’s compound, stolen their cash and made my getaway in a plane. “Drive” by The Cars plays through the speakers as I get behind the wheel for the first time. That first ride in a new “GTA” still hits different. This time, it’s down a rainy road, lit by the glow of warm lights. It’s nostalgic and new at the same time. Yes, my boss knows this is happening. And no, I do not have my driver’s license in real life. But given that “Grand Theft Auto” is such a cultural phenomenon, I was given the green light to chronicle my adventures behind the virtual wheel. For the uninitiated, “GTA” is one of the biggest entertainment franchises in history. Fans of the property have been waiting 13 years for Rockstar Games, the game’s publisher, to release its new installment. The adventure series almost always involves vehicle driving (and sometimes robbery), heist missions and exploring fictional cities that are modeled after real-world places. To prepare for the game, I clocked over 700 hours in “Red Dead Redemption 2,” Rockstar’s previous major release. The new installment of “GTA VI” clearly carries shades of everything that made “RDR2” mesmerizing and addicting. From the reactive nonplayable characters (NPCs) — characters players don’t even control and only sometimes interact with — to the lifelike graphics. “GTA VI,” however, feels even more alive and almost overstimulating. There’s so much happening at once, both to you as a player and the world around. You can also, for the first time, play as both the male and female leads. Jason Duval (a male) and Lucia Caminos (a female), the protagonists, are a couple that find themselves “in the middle of a criminal conspiracy” across the fictional state of Leonida (inspired by Florida). Here’s a play-by-play of the chaos that ensued in my first few hours of gaming. Hour 1 It’s chore time! This game is low-key turning into a drywall installation simulator. I just fed my snake, and I am hanging drywall in my bedroom. The snake’s name is Dolores BTW. And now I am painting. I got to choose between three colors: a blue, green and peach. I went with peach. I am thinking about stealing a boat. Do I steal a boat? Wait. The boat has scuba gear on it. Are we going scuba diving? We are going scuba diving. OK, stole the boat. We’re going offshore to get to deeper water to dive! UHHH, SOMETHING JUST EXPLODED IN THE WATER. OH, THERE IS A BOAT ON FIRE AND A BODY FLOATING IN THE WATER. I’ve encountered a shark. Oh, he got me. But I SURVIVED. First near-death experience, check. Hour 2 There is also a tattoo parlor in Vice City. I do not have a lot of funds, so we gotta go cheap. I am plunging some girl’s sink. My man at the auto shop just fixed the engine of my car and is throwing in a respray for free. What color should I go with? Update: I went with hot pink. Oops. I already messed up the brand-new paint job on a drive less than a mile later. I also hit a guy in an electric wheelchair, caused three cars to spin out, and now I’m being dragged down the street by a car towing a boat. An inevitability in this game: I’m being apprehended by law enforcement. Hour 3 I realized I need to buy this gun to do the next mission, so I am taking $500 out of my house stash (I now have $1,980 stashed away). I think we need to start making some money. I am going to have to try and steal another car because I don’t feel like spending money on getting my car out of the pound. Welp. I’ve been ambushed and am now fistfighting three men I allegedly wronged in the game intro. “Everybody Have Fun Tonight” by Wang Chung is blasting as I knock them out, loot them and made at least $200. Now I am stealing their truck. First mission, going to a grow house. “HOT TO GO!” is now on the radio. I need to keep babygirl Jason hydrated. But I realized I have been driving the wrong way for a mile. Just made $150 stealing a car … that rate seems low? I’m off to pick out a new outfit for Jason. First real mission complete. I am sweaty and anxious. Something I didn’t expect to be doing today: chasing an iguana. Back on the more typical “GTA” grind: I stole a beat-up car next to a “vagrant camp” that seemed out of the cops’ sight. Now I am going to see about getting my hot pink babygirl car out of the pound. Oh, my God, I forgot to take off my gun before I walked into the impound. I have been arrested again. I lost $650. So far, my main takeaway from “GTA 6”: Every time you are trying to make a decision, something else happens that makes you want to do another thing. Stole a little white vespa. Now I am taking pictures in the police department parking lot to see how much it costs to get my babygirl pink car back. Update: I GOT MY CAR BACK! It only took breaking into the impound lot... I need to feed Dolores, again.
